_readme: THE SYSTEMS PANEL MANIFEST LAID AGAINST THE ENGINE'S REQUEST MODEL. TWO LISTS THAT HAD NEVER
BEEN COMPARED UNTIL 2026-09-13.
⛔ THIS FILE IS THE ONLY AUTHORED PART OF THE RECONCILIATION AND IT IS CHECKED IN BOTH
DIRECTIONS, exactly like SACRED{} and the Sacred host list: every panel leaf read off the
running Mock must appear in `panel`, and every field on the engine's request model must be
either the target of a panel row or declared in `engine_only`. A row that drifts out of
either list turns the census RED rather than quietly shrinking it.
⛔ NEITHER SIDE IS TYPED HERE. The panel side is read off window.DATUMAE_MODEL_SCHEDULE in a
real browser; the engine side is read off the running pydantic model. This file only says
what each pairing IS.
BUCKETS:
ENGINE_HAS      - the panel shows it and the engine has a field for it. `engine` names it.
ENGINE_LACKS    - the panel shows it and THE ENGINE HAS NOWHERE TO PUT IT. A build.
ALT_SPELLING    - a second spelling of another row's answer (a date beside an age, a monthly
cadence beside an annual figure). Not a separate model input; `same_as`
names the row it restates. A control here still has to agree with its twin.
DERIVED_DISPLAY - computed for the screen from answers already given, or derived inside the
engine from another field. Nothing to send.
CONFIG          - selects WHICH fields exist rather than being one of them.
MACHINERY       - infrastructure the user has no opinion about.
UI_STATE        - panel bookkeeping. Never leaves the browser.
PANEL_SILENT    - (engine_only) the engine accepts it and NO panel row shows it. This is the
bucket nobody had ever looked at.

planMode.note: Solo or joint. Decides whether the co_architect_* fields exist at all, which is why the payload gate had to learn to enter dual.

co.retirementAge.note: ⛔ The engine ACCEPTS it and the product NEVER ASKS for it — no door refuses on the co-architect's retirement date. Clause 1 asymmetry. A BUILD, NEVER A DELETE (law 191).

co.planThroughAge.note: ⛔ Filled by a MIRROR that copies the primary's plan-through age, so two people are modelled as dying at the same age — against the engine's own field description, 'stated, never assumed equal'. Collapses the survivor window to zero.

co.claimAge.note: ⛔ Pre-selected in live markup and declared kind:'derived'. Nobody picks it.

tax.stateTax.note: The engine derives the state rate from location; the panel shows it back so the user can see what their answer implied.

pensionAmount.note: Household total of the two pension rows below.

pensionPrimaryAmount.note: A pension rides in as an account whose annual_contribution carries the annual income.

pensionCola.note: Household summary of the two per-person COLA rows.

pensionColaPrimary.mode.note: mode 'not_sure' is an honest empty state — it must send nothing, never 0.

pensionColaPrimary.rate.note: ⚠️ PERCENT ON SCREEN, FRACTION ON THE WIRE. 2 means 2%; the engine bounds 0..0.2. 0.2% sent unconverted arrives as 20%, sits ON the bound and PASSES.

ss.claimAge.note: ⛔ Pre-selected in live markup. Nobody picks it.

ss.haircut.note: ⛔ The engine defaults 0.0 — it assumes Social Security is never cut — and nothing on the live product shows that the position was taken. Right value, wrong address.

healthcare.preMedicare.note: Monthly on screen, annual on the wire.

healthcare.inflation.note: ⛔⛔ NO HEALTHCARE INFLATION EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THE ENGINE — measured 2026-09-13 across every module. healthcare_annual sits FLAT forever, and because the engine models real dollars that silently asserts healthcare inflates at exactly CPI. ⚠️ The panel's 4.5%/yr is NOMINAL; the field the engine needs is EXCESS OVER CPI (~2-2.5%), or general inflation is double-counted.

allocation.equity.note: ⛔⛔ THE PRIORITY OF THE ARC. The engine has NO allocation field; it runs a hardcoded glide (GLIDE_START_EQ 0.79 -> GLIDE_END_EQ 0.50 over 30 years, CASH_PCT 0.03) sourced to the Captain's own workbook cells I&A B265-B267. ⚠️ An equity_pct PARAMETER exists but feeds only the MEAN RETURN; volatility comes from glide_vol() which reads the constants and ignores it — so wiring the obvious parameter opens the door HALFWAY. Two defaults already disagree: income 0.80, models 0.79.

allocation.cash.note: Same wall as allocation.equity. Already declared kind:'unsourced' in the engine's constant ledger with a note saying the user cannot touch it.

cape.note: A world fact. Needs a value PLUS an as-of date PLUS a staleness policy, never a bare number.

bridgeMode.note: Already a labelled dropdown in the Mock. Right value, wrong address — the default lives in schemas.py instead of on the panel.

marketModel.note: House default Datumae Blend, applied by the panel as a labelled assumption — never by a class='active' attribute.

contributions.accounts.ira.continueAfter.note: AccountInput carries type, balance, annual_contribution and rule_of_55_eligible. There is no 'keep contributing after retirement' flag; contributions accrue during accumulation only.

contributions.accounts.workplace.continu.note: Same gap as the IRA row.

contributions.accounts.taxable.continueA.note: The Mock says taxable CAN continue after retirement. The engine cannot express it.

contributionGrowth.note: ⛔ The engine models contributions as a LEVEL annuity — portfolio x growth + contribution x (growth-1)/r — so they never escalate. A 401(k) contribution tracks the limit and the salary, and the limit rises most years. The control already exists in the Mock at 0-8%, step 0.25, default 2%. Must accept 0 for a user who wants flat.

machinery.trialsPerModel.note: Shown for transparency; the engine takes one trial count.

machinery.totalPaths.note: trials x models, for the screen.

machinery.overrides.note: Reports whether any spreadsheet override is in play.

floorLoad.note: ⭐ THE DOOR LANDED 2026-09-13. Until then compute_bedrock tested all_survived as a literal, so the Ceiling was shapeable from Python and the Floor was not shapeable at any price. The engine now also returns floor_notches saying which positions leave a range to show.

specReviewed.note: Whether the user has acknowledged the panel. Never leaves the browser.

current_ss_plan.note: Marks one SS-matrix cell as the household's current plan. The SS matrix has its own surface; no Systems Panel row shows it.

custom_weights.note: Per-model blend weights for the Custom Matrix option. RULED RETIRED alongside market_outlook 'custom' — the five-button control replaces it. Still on the model.

accum_years_override.note: YEARFRAC-precise accumulation years, for exact spreadsheet cell matching. A development affordance, never a user input.

portfolio_at_retirement_override.note: Exact portfolio FV from a spreadsheet cell. Same status as accum_years_override.
